backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first ~300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value from the step counter each iteration and writing it into the Muon param group before the optimizer step. Leave all other Muon settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. This cuts optimizer overhead per step, so the fixed 300 s budget buys more training steps. Keep the same quintic coefficients and all other hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations for Muon

backlog.spec: Scale each Muon matrix update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so that tall and wide matrices get comparable update RMS, instead of the current unscaled orthogonalized update. Apply it in the Muon step right after orthogonalization and keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 for the first test.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon update scaling

backlog.spec: Add decoupled weight decay of 0.01 (scaled by the current LR multiplier) to the AdamW-managed groups: token embeddings, lm_head, and per-layer scalars. Currently these groups get no decay. Muon's WEIGHT_DECAY=0.2 stays as is.
backlog.title: Light decoupled weight decay on Adam parameters

backlog.spec: Set the Adam beta1 for the embedding, lm_head, and scalar groups to 0.9 while keeping beta2 at 0.95. This makes Adam react faster to gradient changes over the short 300 s run. Muon is unaffected.
backlog.title: Lower beta1 for Adam groups

backlog.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward pass and before optimizer steps, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters. This guards against loss spikes at the high embedding and scalar LRs.
backlog.title: Gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to zero over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO fraction of the time budget. Keep the warmup and the peak LRs unchanged. The LR multiplier is a function of elapsed time over the budget.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the last 70% of the 300 s budget. Keep the peak LRs, warmup (0), and FINAL_LR_FRAC (0) unchanged. This is a single-constant change.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so that all LR groups ramp linearly from 0 to their peak over the first 3% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. The current schedule starts at full LR immediately, and this tests whether a brief ramp stabilizes early Muon updates.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the LR decays to 10% of its initial value at the end of the budget rather than to zero. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5. Tests whether a small residual LR helps the final tokens.
backlog.title: Nonzero final LR fraction

backlog.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.2 for the per-layer scalar parameters (attention and MLP residual scalars and similar). The current value is very high for scalars, so this checks whether they are destabilizing training. All other LRs stay the same.
backlog.title: Lower scalar LR

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 for the Muon matrix parameters, keeping the Adam LRs unchanged. This probes whether the Muon group is under-driven in the short time budget.
backlog.title: Higher Muon matrix LR

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (about 262K tokens per optimizer step) so the 300 s budget yields roughly twice as many optimizer steps. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic unchanged, so accumulation falls to half.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch size

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 (about 1M tokens per optimizer step), which increases gradient accuracy at the cost of fewer steps. Keep the LRs unchanged for the first test and let gradient accumulation increase to match.
backlog.title: Larger total batch size

backlog.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 for the first half of the time budget and switch to 2**19 for the second half. Recompute the gradient accumulation steps at the switch point. This gives fast early progress and a stable late phase.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 52 so model_dim stays near 512 with 25% more layers. Keep HEAD_DIM, WINDOW_PATTERN, and all other settings unchanged. Tests whether extra depth helps more than the lost width.
backlog.title: Deeper and narrower model

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU MLP. Use a hidden width of about 8/3 times model_dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, so the parameter count stays close to the current MLP. Keep the rest of the block unchanged.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits before the cross-entropy: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). This bounds logit magnitude and can stabilize training at the high LRs. Apply it in the forward pass for training and evaluation alike, without touching the evaluation call.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Normalize queries and keys with RMSNorm over the head dimension before rotary embeddings, and add a learnable per-head scalar gain on the query side initialized to 1. This stabilizes attention logits at high LR.
backlog.title: QK-norm with learnable per-head gain

backlog.spec: Increase the RoPE base frequency from 10000 to 100000 for the rotary embeddings. This changes the positional frequency range, which can help longer effective context in the sliding window layers. No other changes.
backlog.title: Higher rotary base

backlog.spec: Keep a copy of the normalized token embedding x0 and mix it into each block's residual stream through a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0.1, in addition to the existing residual path. This gives every layer direct access to the token identity signal.
backlog.title: Input embedding skip into every layer

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSLL" so half of the layers use full context. Test whether more full-context attention improves val_bpb enough to offset the extra compute.
backlog.title: Denser full-attention window pattern

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary z-loss of 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training cross-entropy to keep the output logit normalizer near zero. Apply it only in the training loss, not in evaluation.
backlog.title: Logit z-loss regularizer

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model weights with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Run the final model evaluation with the EMA weights swapped in. Training dynamics are unchanged. The evaluation call itself is not modified.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for evaluation

backlog.spec: Train for the first 30% of the time budget with a shorter sequence length of half the full context, doubling it afterward. Keep the total tokens per optimizer step fixed by adjusting the batch dimension. This cheapens early steps and lets the model learn fast before full-length attention.
backlog.title: Sequence length curriculum

backlog.spec: Make sure attention uses torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention with the causal or sliding-window mask in a fused backend, and enable TF32 matmul and cuDNN benchmark mode at startup. This raises throughput per second of the fixed budget without changing the math.
backlog.title: Fused attention and compile check

backlog.spec: Enable gradient checkpointing on each transformer block so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE can go to 128 within 40 GB. Gradient accumulation halves to match the same TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE. Fewer, larger micro-batches should improve GPU utilization even though recomputation adds some cost.
backlog.title: Activation checkpointing for larger device batch

backlog.spec: Remove the separate lm_head weight and reuse the token embedding matrix as the output projection (logits = x @ wte.weight.T). Scale the shared embedding init to std about 0.02 or follow the existing init, and scale the final hidden state by 1/sqrt(model_dim) before the tied projection so logit magnitudes stay stable. Put the shared matrix in the embedding Adam group using EMBEDDING_LR, and drop the UNEMBEDDING_LR group. This removes about 2*vocab*dim parameters and one optimizer group. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Tie input and output embeddings

backlog.spec: Capture the value projection v from layer 0 and, in every later attention layer, mix it into the current value as v_l = lambda_l * v_l + (1 - lambda_l) * v_0, where lambda_l is a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5 and trained with SCALAR_LR. Layer 0 is unchanged. The extra cost is one elementwise blend per layer, with no new matmuls. Keep the sliding-window pattern and rotary embeddings as they are.
backlog.title: ResFormer-style first-layer value residual

backlog.spec: Apply RoPE only to the first half of each head's channels and leave the second half unrotated (NoPE), so attention can match on content as well as position. Implement by slicing q and k into rotary and pass-through parts before the rotation, then concatenating them back. The rotation frequencies are computed for the rotary half only. Nothing else changes, and the compute cost is essentially the same.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embeddings on half of each head

backlog.spec: Scale the MATRIX_LR of each transformer block by a factor that decreases with depth, for example lr_l = MATRIX_LR * (0.8 ** (l / (DEPTH - 1)))... so the first block gets the full rate and the last gets 0.8 of it. Implement this by creating one Muon param group per layer with its own lr, and keep the existing momentum, weight decay and Newton-Schulz settings. The warmdown multiplier is applied to all groups in the same way as now.
backlog.title: Depth-wise learning rate decay for Muon matrices

backlog.spec: Keep the Adam-style groups (embedding, lm_head, scalars) on the current linear warmdown that starts at 50% of the budget. For the Muon matrix group only, begin the warmdown later, at 70% of the budget, and decay it to 0 by the end, so the matrix parameters keep learning at full rate for longer. Compute the two multipliers from elapsed time fraction as separate functions, and apply them to their respective param groups each step.
backlog.title: Separate warmdown for Muon and Adam groups

backlog.spec: The metric is bits per byte, but training minimizes per-token cross-entropy, so tokens with many UTF-8 bytes count the same as tokens with few. Precompute for each vocabulary id the number of bytes its decoded string produces, using the tokenizer that train.py already has. In the loss, weight each target token's cross-entropy by its byte length divided by the batch mean byte length, so the gradient matches the bpb objective. Normalize the weights so the average scale is unchanged, and keep the logging in the usual units.
backlog.title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy aligned with bits per byte

backlog.spec: Replace AdamW on the embedding and lm_head parameters with a Lion update: keep one momentum buffer per parameter, compute update = sign(beta1 * m + (1 - beta1) * grad), apply the parameter step as lr * update plus decoupled weight decay, then set m = beta2 * m + (1 - beta2) * grad. Use beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99 and scale the learning rates by about 0.3 of their Adam values, because sign updates have unit magnitude. Scalars and Muon matrices are unchanged.
backlog.title: Lion-style sign update for embedding and output Adam groups

backlog.spec: Set the Muon weight decay to 0 at the start and increase it linearly to WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 by 60% of the time budget, then hold it constant. Early in training the weights should move freely, and later decay acts as a regularizer that shrinks the weights toward the constrained norm. Update the decay value of the Muon param group at each step from the elapsed time fraction. Leave the Adam groups and the rest of the schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Ramped Muon weight decay

backlog.spec: Store the Muon momentum buffers and the Newton-Schulz working matrices in bfloat16 instead of float32, and cast the gradient to bf16 before the momentum update, then cast the orthogonalized update back to the parameter dtype before applying it. This lowers memory traffic in the optimizer step, which is a small but real share of step time, so more steps fit into the fixed 300 s. Keep the Adam state in float32 and keep the same learning rates.
backlog.title: Bf16 Muon momentum buffers for speed

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of every attention block and MLP block to exactly zero, so each layer starts as the identity and the residual stream begins from the embedding alone. Also multiply the final logits by a fixed factor of 1/sqrt(model_dim / 256) before the softmax, to keep the initial logit scale comparable across model widths. Keep the Muon update for these matrices; the zero init only affects the starting point. Everything else is the same.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized residual branches with logit scaling

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block from sequential residuals (x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x))) to a parallel form: x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), with one shared RMSNorm feeding both branches. Keep the existing per-layer residual scalars and the window pattern unchanged. This keeps FLOPs roughly constant while removing one serial dependency per layer, so it may raise throughput under the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP block

backlog.spec: After the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization in the Muon step, track an Adam-like running second moment of each output row of the orthogonalized update (beta2 around 0.95, eps 1e-8) and divide the update by its square root, then rescale so the update's overall RMS matches the current Muon scaling. Leave Newton-Schulz iteration count, momentum, and weight decay unchanged. This equalizes per-neuron update magnitudes across the matrix parameters.
backlog.title: NorMuon-style row normalization after Newton-Schulz

backlog.spec: Add a second token embedding table of size vocab by model_dim, shared across layers but with a separate learned gate per layer initialized to zero. In each attention layer, add gate_l times this token embedding to the value vectors v before attention (after the projection and reshape, matching shapes). The table is looked up from the same input ids, so the extra cost is one gather per forward pass. Train the table with the embedding Adam group.
backlog.title: Per-layer token value embeddings

backlog.spec: Replace the plain mean cross-entropy with a focal-style weighted version: for each token compute p = exp(-ce), then weight its loss by (1 - p)^0.5 with the weight detached from the graph, and average over tokens with the same normalization as before. Tokens the model already predicts well contribute less, and hard tokens get more gradient. Do not change the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Focal-style per-token loss weighting

backlog.spec: Detect the BOS token id that already separates documents in the training token stream. Build a per-position document id by cumulative sum of BOS occurrences within each sequence. In attention, mask out keys whose document id differs from the query's (combine with the existing causal and sliding-window masks). Use the mask via an additive bias or a block mask; if the fused attention path cannot take it, fall back to the masked explicit path only for training. This prevents cross-document leakage during training.
backlog.title: Document-boundary attention isolation

backlog.spec: During training only, skip each transformer block's residual update with a per-step Bernoulli drop. The drop probability rises linearly with layer index from 0 at layer 0 to 0.1 at the last layer, and the kept residual branches are not rescaled. Use the standard full forward pass at evaluation. This reduces average compute per step so more optimizer steps fit in the 300 s budget, while acting as a mild regularizer.
backlog.title: Stochastic layer dropping with depth-scaled rate

backlog.spec: Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0 and the current warmdown start point (50 percent of the time budget). Replace the linear decay of the learning-rate multiplier in the warmdown with a sqrt-shaped decay: multiplier = 1 - sqrt(progress), where progress runs from 0 at the warmdown start to 1 at the end, then clamp at FINAL_LR_FRAC. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups. This keeps learning rate higher for longer early in the decay and drops it sharply near the end.
backlog.title: Square-root warmdown shape

backlog.spec: Move the token embedding and lm_head weight matrices out of the Adam groups and into a Muon group, using the same orthogonalized update with a dedicated learning rate of roughly 0.02 and the same momentum and weight decay settings as the matrix Muon group. Keep the Adam groups for norms and scalars only. Because the embedding is vocab by model_dim, Newton-Schulz runs on the transposed shape if needed. This is a bold change that tests whether orthogonalized updates help the two largest matrices.
backlog.title: Muon on embedding and output head

backlog.spec: Add an RMSNorm after each attention output and after each MLP output, before the residual addition, while keeping the existing pre-norms. Use learnable gain initialized to 1 on these post-norms, or a parameter-free norm if simpler. This adds negligible compute and bounds the magnitude each branch writes into the residual stream, which may stabilize training at high matrix learning rates.
backlog.title: Extra post-branch RMSNorm (sandwich norm)

backlog.spec: In the Muon optimizer step, group all matrix parameters that share a shape, stack their gradients or momentum buffers into one tensor, and run the Newton-Schulz iteration and parameter update once per group with batched matmuls instead of once per parameter. The math per parameter is unchanged. This reduces kernel launch overhead per step, so the same 300 s budget allows more optimizer steps.
backlog.title: Batched Muon update across same-shape matrices

backlog.spec: Share parameters across layer pairs (ALBERT-style): build only DEPTH//2 unique transformer blocks and run each block twice in sequence, so layers 0 and 1 use one set of attention and MLP weights, layers 2 and 3 another, and so on. Keep per-layer RMSNorm and the per-layer scalar residual gains unshared so each pass still has its own scaling. Spend the freed parameter budget by setting ASPECT_RATIO to about 80 so model_dim grows while keeping the same HEAD_DIM. Leave the optimizer grouping logic intact, but make sure the shared Muon matrices are registered once, not twice, in the parameter groups.
backlog.title: Cross-layer weight sharing with wider blocks

backlog.spec: Replace the time-based LR warmdown for the embedding, unembedding and scalar Adam groups with schedule-free AdamW (Defazio et al.): keep a fast iterate z updated by Adam, a slow averaged iterate x updated as x = (1 - 1/t_c) x + (1/t_c) z, and evaluate and train the gradient at the interpolation y = (1 - beta1) z + beta1 x, with beta1 = 0.9 for these groups. Set the LR to the current constant peak value with no decay. Keep Muon on the matrix parameters with its existing schedule. At the end of training, load x into the model weights before the evaluation call. Do not touch the evaluation call itself.
backlog.title: Schedule-free AdamW for the Adam groups

backlog.spec: Add a second embedding table indexed by a hash of the current and previous token: idx = (prev_token * 1000003 + cur_token) mod 4096, with a 4096 x model_dim table initialized to zero. Add its output to the token embedding before the first layer and scale it by a learnable scalar initialized to 0. This gives the model cheap bigram statistics without extra attention layers. Use the Adam embedding LR for this table. The first position uses prev_token = 0. Keep the rest of the forward pass and the parameter count otherwise unchanged apart from this table.
backlog.title: Hashed bigram embedding added to token embeddings

backlog.spec: After scaled dot-product attention and before the output projection, multiply each head's output by a sigmoid gate computed from the block input: g = sigmoid(x @ W_g) with W_g a linear map from model_dim to n_heads, initialized so the gate starts near 1 (bias init of +2, weights zero). Apply the gate per head, broadcast over head_dim. Put W_g in the Muon matrix group like the other attention weights, or in the Adam group if the shape is awkward. This adds only a small projection per layer and lets each head suppress its own contribution in a context-dependent way.
backlog.title: Per-head sigmoid output gate on attention

backlog.spec: Add a lightweight auxiliary head that predicts the token two steps ahead. Concatenate the final hidden state at position t with the embedding of token t+1 through a single linear map back to model_dim, then apply the shared lm_head to get logits for token t+2. Add this cross-entropy to the main loss with weight 0.1 during training only. Drop the auxiliary head from the forward path during evaluation and final logit computation, so the evaluation call and output are identical in form to the baseline. The added compute should be small relative to the transformer blocks, so the step count should stay close to baseline.
backlog.title: Auxiliary multi-token prediction head during training only

backlog.spec: For the embedding, unembedding and scalar Adam groups only, apply the MARS variance-reduction correction before the Adam update. Keep the previous step's gradient g_prev per parameter. Form the corrected gradient c_t = g_t + gamma * (beta1 / (1 - beta1)) * (g_t - g_prev), with gamma = 0.025 and beta1 = the existing Adam beta1. Clip c_t so its norm does not exceed 1 times the norm of g_t, then feed c_t into the standard Adam first and second moment updates. Store g_prev after each step. Leave Muon matrices unchanged. This is one extra buffer per Adam parameter and no extra forward or backward passes.
backlog.title: MARS variance-reduced gradients for Adam groups

backlog.spec: During training only, drop input token embeddings at random: for each position, zero the embedding vector with probability 0.05 and multiply surviving embeddings by 1/(1 - 0.05) so the expected scale is unchanged. Apply this to the output of the token embedding table before the first transformer block. Do not apply dropout inside attention or the MLP. Disable the dropout when the model is in evaluation mode so the evaluation path is unchanged. This is a cheap regularizer aimed at reducing reliance on individual tokens while the model is still in a relatively data-rich regime.
backlog.title: Input token dropout with embedding scaling

backlog.spec: Use label-smoothed cross-entropy for the training loss only, with smoothing epsilon = 0.05 over the full vocabulary: target distribution is 0.95 on the true token and 0.05 spread uniformly across all vocabulary entries. Compute the loss with torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, targets, label_smoothing=0.05). Keep the evaluation loss computed exactly as in the existing code so the reported metric is unchanged. This is a single-line change to the training loss and adds no compute or memory.
backlog.title: Label smoothing on the training cross-entropy

backlog.spec: Overlap host-to-device data movement with the forward and backward pass. Keep the batch generator unchanged in what it yields, but wrap it so the next batch is fetched and copied to the GPU on a separate CUDA stream while the current step runs: allocate pinned host buffers, use non_blocking=True copies, and call torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(copy_stream) before using the batch. Keep the number of tokens per step and the sampling order identical to the baseline. This is a throughput change only, aimed at squeezing a few more optimizer steps into the fixed 300-second budget.
backlog.title: Asynchronous pinned-memory data prefetch

backlog.spec: During the final 30% of training, when the LR is in warmdown, keep a running uniform average of model weights sampled every 50 optimizer steps (a Stochastic Weight Averaging-style running mean over snapshots, not an exponential moving average). Keep the average in bf16 on GPU to save memory. When training ends, copy the averaged weights into the model before the final evaluation call and leave the evaluation call itself untouched. Measure nothing extra in the loop beyond this averaging. This differs from a per-step EMA by using sparse uniform snapshots taken where the LR is decaying, which tends to land in flatter regions.
backlog.title: Stride-averaged checkpoint ensemble over the warmdown

memo:
Incumbent mean_adjusted is 1.1145 over 16 runs. Every slot has one run, so gaps near 0.002 may be noise. Nothing has been accepted yet.

Helped slightly, but all rejected: learnable query gain (1.1116, -0.0029), gradient clipping (1.1131, -0.0014), a separate Muon warmdown (1.1132, -0.0013), MATRIX_LR 0.06 (1.1124, -0.0021). All are cheap and add no compute per step. Weight decay 0.01 on the AdamW groups was -0.0005, which is likely noise.

Hurt: depth 10 (+0.0196), a 2^20 token batch (+0.0671), warmup 0.03 (+0.0095), a value residual (+0.0080), SwiGLU (+0.0041), warmdown 0.7 (+0.0017), a weight EMA (+0.0012). Anything that adds compute per step or cuts the step count looks bad under the fixed 300 s budget.

Slots 7 and 14 failed to patch, and slots 11 and 15 crashed. The 2^18 batch and the Muon momentum warmup are still untested.

Next: retry those two with patches that apply. Then stack query gain, clipping, the Muon warmdown and MATRIX_LR 0.06, and replicate the stack against noise.
